clue.text: The world of academe and literature

parts.note: academe, the university world, is shortened to uni
verse is poetry, a branch of literature

explanation.surface: A remark about the cloistered sphere of scholars and books.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, so it can stand for the whole world or cosmos.

clue.text: With tricks on the pitch, men with guts mix it

indicators.note: to mix it is to stir things up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Brave footballers who use skill on the pitch also get stuck into the physical side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix it' rearranges MEN and GUTS; 'with' between them is a link. In football a nutmeg is playing the ball through an opponent's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In football slang a nutmeg is a trick of passing the ball between a defender's legs.

clue.text: See a sign giving clearance

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see, used in references
an indication is a sign or hint

explanation.surface: An instruction to look for a signal that permission has been granted.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from the Latin vide, as in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindication clears a person of blame, so it is a clearance of their name.

clue.text: Frank drinks toast

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group
a single slice of toasted bread

explanation.surface: A man named Frank drinks to someone's health.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'Frank' looks like a name and 'toast' a salute, but each word is a separate sense of the answer; a slice of toast is a round in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers outspoken speech, a group order of drinks at a pub, and a slice of toast.

clue.text: Entrance charge, covering an hour, show hasn't started

indicators.note: the show that results is not yet started, so the built word loses its opening letter
the outer word goes round, covering, the hour's letter

parts.note: a rental is a charge paid for hiring something
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Admission fees are explained while a performance is delayed by an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts HR inside RENTAL to give RENTHRAL, and 'show hasn't started' drops its first letter. 'Entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them spellbound, which is what enthralling them means.

clue.text: Instigate prank, interrupting gym class

indicators.note: one piece breaking into another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: PT, physical training, is the school gym lesson
a romp is a boisterous frolic or prank

explanation.surface: A pupil starts some horseplay in the middle of PE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt something is to cause or instigate it.

clue.text: Letter from abroad recently triggered mas an interest in stamps

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A foreign letter that arrived not long ago sparked a hobby in stamp collecting.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'mas' is an OCR slip for 'as', a link word along with 'triggered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is the collecting and study of postage stamps, a hobby or interest.

clue.text: Old hat is not acceptable

definitions.meaning: old hat means unfashionable, no longer in style
not acceptable, as in a suggestion that is ruled ...

explanation.surface: A dated hat is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unfashionable and excluded, as with an option that is ruled out.

clue.text: Over time, fatso finally drops down 10 stone

indicators.note: the letter falls lower in the column, moving later in the word
in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, a full stop or era

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of fatso

explanation.surface: A fat person loses ten stone over a period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' puts PERIOD above T, giving PERIODT; then 'drops down' moves the O (the last letter of 'fatso') lower. '10 stone' looks like a weight; 10 is the cross-reference and 'stone' the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is an olive-green gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: This can bring about stuttering and woe

definitions.text: This can bring about stuttering and woe

indicators.note: to bring something about can mean to turn it round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tricky phrase can leave a speaker stammering and miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring about' rearranges STUTTERING and WOE; the whole clue also describes the answer, with 'This can' pointing at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-twister is a phrase hard to say quickly, so it makes people stumble over words.

clue.text: Stop in time

definitions.meaning: a full stop, the punctuation mark
an era or span of time

explanation.surface: Halt at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a full stop in punctuation and also a length of time such as an era.

clue.text: Epic poem penned by, perhaps, Odysseus

indicators.note: the answer is penned, enclosed, within the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A long heroic poem maybe written by the wandering hero of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody in ancient Greece was a section of epic poetry recited in one sitting.

clue.text: Heterosexual stooge

definitions.meaning: a man who is attracted to women, straight being slang for heterosexual
the comedian's partner who feeds lines to the funny one

explanation.surface: A heterosexual sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a heterosexual male and also a comic's foil who sets up the jokes.

clue.text: A doctor wearing back to front oval shoe

indicators.note: the doctor wearing the other piece has it around him, so he sits inside
back to front means the oval word is read in reverse

parts.note: an ellipse is an oval shape

explanation.surface: A doctor puts on an oval shoe the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' turns ELLIPSE into ESPILLE, and 'wearing' puts A DR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: This will mirror imp held up by cleric Jell

indicators.note: held by the other word, so the reversed piece sits inside it

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest, a cleric

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an elf is a small mischievous sprite, like an imp

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite is lifted aloft by a clergyman to show its reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELF into FLE and 'held' puts it inside RECTOR. The printed 'Jell' is an OCR stray with no part in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflector is a surface that throws back light or images, so it mirrors them.

clue.text: Ceremony requiring correct pronunciation

indicators.note: pronunciation means the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: right means correct

explanation.surface: A formal occasion where everyone must say things properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ritual or solemn ceremony.

clue.text: One redcap assigned to one group of soldiers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a redcap is a British military policeman, an MP
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A military policeman is posted to a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red caps.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.

clue.text: A sailor, I will be accepted by Silas …

indicators.note: taken in by the surname, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: Silas Marner is the title character of George Eliot's novel

explanation.surface: A seaman says he will be welcomed aboard by a man named Silas.
explanation.walkthrough: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel, so 'Silas' gives MARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who sails.

clue.text: Unreliable and less popular way to travel

definitions.meaning: untrustworthy, as a shady business is
taking a night flight, fewer people choosing to travel through the night

explanation.surface: An undependable and unfashionable means of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a disreputable trader and, read literally, flying through the night.

clue.text: … my radar's out of order — it's up in the rigging

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order, so they are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: A sailor complains the radar has broken and sits high in the ship's masts.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a yard, the spar that holds a sail up on a mast.

clue.text: This protects beehive, for instance, out in the rain

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something keeps a towering hairdo safe when one goes out in wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THE RAIN; 'in' is a link. A beehive is a tall bouffant hairstyle, not a home for bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet holds a hairstyle such as a beehive in place and keeps it tidy.

clue.text: Nan lamented being rejected by state

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother, as is gran

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: rued means regretted or lamented

explanation.surface: A grandmother grieved at being turned down by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' turns RUED into DEUR; 'state' is pomp, as in lying in state, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: State in the sense of ceremonial pomp, as in lying in state, matches splendour or magnificence.

clue.text: Composite trouble had come back

indicators.note: coming back means the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worry one had has returned.

clue.text: Propriety largely required in scenery

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its tail

parts.note: decorum is propriety, good manners

explanation.surface: Good manners are mostly expected on the stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last two letters of DECORUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor can mean the scenery and furnishings of a stage set.

clue.text: Astronomer's security guard?

parts.note: a guard on the late shift, or whimsically a stargazer who keeps an eye on the night sky

explanation.surface: Who protects the stargazer?
explanation.definitionFit: A guard who patrols premises at night, which suits an astronomer's nocturnal watching too.

clue.text: Torture used within country's borders

the borders of the country name are its first and last letters, which go

explanation.walkthrough: 'within' and 'borders' keep what lies inside EGYPT's first and last letters. Gyp is British slang for pain, as in giving someone gyp.

clue.text: Transposed by proxy? That's correct

indicators.note: transposed means the two pieces swap places from their clue order

parts.note: pro, as in pro tem, means acting for; as a prefix it means on behalf of, by proxy
per means by, as in per post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transposed' puts the piece for 'proxy' before the piece for 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means right or correct, as in the proper way to do something.

clue.text: Mother finds charge for clothing in vogue steep

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: one piece clothing another wraps around it

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price
in means fashionable, in vogue

explanation.surface: A mother discovers the price of fashionable clothes is steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts IN inside RATE. 'steep' is the verb, to soak, not the adjective for high.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep food in a liquid is to soak or marinate it.
